To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in the defect case the AC conductivity is a constant at low frequencies, that the baryon quasi-particle dispersion is a simple linear function of the momentum, and that the Drude relaxation time is a linear function of the mass-squared over density.

the physical response functions of strongly-coupled, massive quantum liquids are determined by a single parameter, the mass to density ratio, and that these liquids are characterized by a crossover between a meson-dominated regime and a baryon-dominated one.

the baryon spectral function has a peak that is located at an energy of order the baryon mass, while the meson spectral function has peaks that are located at energies of order the temperature, and the ratio of the baryonic to the mesonic peak is proportional to the mass-squared over the baryon density.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the spectral properties of a strongly coupled quantum liquid of heavy fermions.
the physical properties of a strongly coupled massive quantum liquid.
the physical response of strongly coupled quantum matter at finite density.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the baryon-charge transport in the strongly coupled regime of QCD at high baryon density is dominated by the mesonic degrees of freedom, and the baryon transport is suppressed by a large mass gap.
we have obtained a new, very simple and very general expression for the AC conductivity of strongly coupled massive matter at finite temperature.
the physical properties of strongly-coupled massive quantum liquids are determined by the mass-to-density ratio, which is a measure of how strongly the baryons are bound.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we provide a new and simple way to compute the spectral functions of massive quantum liquids, which is applicable to a wide range of physical systems, from dense nuclear matter to heavy-ion collisions.
the physical response functions of the strongly-coupled quantum liquids are universal functions of the dimensionless mass-squared to baryon density ratio.
the physical properties of strongly interacting dense quantum liquids are universal and can be expressed in a very simple form.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we can use AdS/CFT to compute physical response functions in strongly coupled quantum liquids, and that we can use these results to learn about the nature of the strongly-coupled quark-gluon plasma at finite baryon density and finite temperature.
the spectral function of strongly coupled quantum liquids is universal and independent of the details of the underlying microscopic model.
the physics of dense, massive, strongly coupled matter at temperatures well below the deconfining phase transition is dominated by a single parameter, the mass-squared over density ratio.
